method.dailySample: one block per calendar day for 365 days, stepping back in exact 7200-block strides (12s slots) from the latest block; the base fee of that single block, not a daily average
method.peakRefinement: every block inspected across a +/-150 block window around a coarse hit, so the reported peak is the true maximum of that ~1 hour window
method.ethPrice: Chainlink ETH/USD aggregator 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 latestRoundData() on mainnet, 8 decimals

gasAnchors.label: now
gasAnchors.why: the latest block at generation time, so the page can say what gas costs right now rather than only what it has cost

gasAnchors.label: high
gasAnchors.why: the busiest moment of the dearest day in the trailing year's daily sample (2026-03-22); a bad day on a normal network, not a crisis

gasAnchors.label: extremely high
gasAnchors.why: the worst moment of the trailing year, during the 2025-10-10 market-wide liquidation event; the network still works, but every write is ~4,500x the median

gasAnchors.label: historical peak
gasAnchors.why: the highest base fee since EIP-1559 went live: the Otherdeed land mint, 2022-05-01. Kept because the ticket asks for a real historical peak and because it is the honest ceiling, even though a 30M-gas-limit chain in 2022 is not the 60M chain of today

notes.medianIsTheAverageDial: Tim's 'average' dial uses the MEDIAN of the daily sample, not the mean. The mean (0.3293 gwei) is dragged up by a handful of spike days and is not what a normal day costs; the median (0.1184 gwei) is.
notes.baseFeeOnly: Every gas figure here is the BASE FEE only. A real transaction also pays a priority fee to be included. The model exposes the priority fee as its own dial rather than baking a guess into these anchors.
notes.preLondon: No anchor predates block 12965000 (EIP-1559). Before that there is no base fee in the header, only per-transaction gas prices, which are not comparable.
